name: Ferrochem AcidWall Pro MK-4 Full Enclosure Suit
description:
Full-body enclosure suit in corroded-mustard yellow with black chemical-resistance banding at all seams. Triple-laminate shell of vulcanized polyimide over woven aramid, with a bonded inner moisture-wicking membrane. Visor hood integrates a filtered air intake mounted left-shoulder. Common on Shelf salvage crews working flooded industrial basements where acid pooling is standard.

Seam tape is factory-applied in neon orange — when it fades to white, the suit's primary seal integrity is compromised. Most Shelf workers ignore this. Wrist and ankle cuffs cinch via ratchet buckles, leaving room for basic chrome cuffs beneath.
functionality: Rated for pH 1–13 splash and immersion up to 40 minutes. Integrated shoulder air-intake runs through a replaceable carbon-block filter cartridge. Ratchet cuff seals accommodate basic chrome prosthetics. Internal BCI port slot on hood collar allows neural comms while fully enclosed.
what_it_says: You work in places that will kill you slowly, and you know exactly how much protection you can actually afford.
story_hooks: A salvager's suit seal tape has been white for three weeks — she can't afford a replacement and is showing early acid-burn scarring on her wrists.
A batch of counterfeit MK-4 suits hit the Shelf market — identical labeling, half the chemical resistance rating, and workers are dying.
Someone found a sealed MK-4 suit in a flooded basement with a body inside — the suit is undamaged, but the person inside died of something else entirely.
